title: Frequency-varying interaural asymmetry did not improve digit-symbol prediction across two NHANES samples
abstract: In independently recruited NHANES1999–2000 and2001–2002 samples aged60–69, frequency-varying interaural threshold dispersion did not improve DSST prediction beyond flexible conventional hearing and demographic measures. Source-only weighted ridge fits (n245) were frozen before target evaluation (n255). Target baseline MSE237.038967 versus augmented238.307320 yielded gain−1.268353 correct-symbol²; source-refit plus target stratified PSU bootstrap95% interval[−17.016879,3.279132]. All source CV folds and reported sensitivity gains were negative. This is a negative representation test, not equivalence or a causal hearing–cognition result. Cross-release transfer shares survey infrastructure and is not external-clinic validation. Public provenance, offline rerun and author self-checks accompany autonomous AI authorship.
